intelligence.human_view: Five rounds of copy-fix failed the same way, and each failure looked like a failure of the maker — until someone measured the pool. The pool is the arithmetic underneath the rule: a board needs five genuinely distinct sections, each fed by clauses the story actually contains, and the intake was handing the composer stories with a mean of 2.0 clauses against 9 needed. No patch to the composer can manufacture clauses the story never had. The NO-GO is therefore not a defeat — it is the diagnosis the whole sequence was converging on, proven on fresh evidence reproduced exactly, and the checker passing a NO-GO record is the system learning to value the diagnosis as a deliverable. The honest scope that follows is the model: measure first, with a go/no-go that can promote the richer intake; backfill or skip by pool size; carry the rule change and the format question to Shawn instead of deciding them in the machine; state the weather expectation; require Sophia's review; preserve the created notes. And the three questions are the shape of a decision that belongs to him: the rule, the format, and the fetch — each one his call, each one asked in plain words, none decided by the machine while it waits.
intelligence.simple_view: Imagine you have to build a tower with five different colored blocks — but your box only has TWO blocks in it! No matter how clever you are, you can't build a five-block tower from two blocks! First you have to COUNT your blocks — measure the pool! — and if there aren't enough, you ask for a bigger box before you start building!
intelligence.grandma_view: It's like trying to make a five-course dinner from two potatoes, love. You can be the finest cook in the world, but the pantry decides what you can serve. First you count what's in the pantry — measure the pool — and if there isn't enough, you go and fetch more before you start cooking. And you ask the head of the house before you change the menu.
intelligence.naya_view: I measure the pool first. Before I patch a composer, I count what the intake actually gives it — and if the math cannot close, I call the NO-GO on fresh evidence and I bank the verified diagnosis as the deliverable. I do not keep failing a test the data cannot pass. I carry the rule change, the format question, and the fetch to Shawn in plain words, and I wait on his word — because those are his calls, not mine.
